text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- An opinion poll reveals that 81.9 percent of those who voted for the ruling Islamist Welfare Party in the last election would vote for them again if there were an election next Sunday.
- Crowds fight each other in the mud to get food given by a businessman in the holy month of Ramadan in the poverty-stricken southeastern province of Diyarbakir.
- Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller gives a sigh of relief as she is cleared by a parliamentary commission of the third and last corruption charge against her.
- Brother of Ugur Mumcu, a secularist journalist murdered four years ago in a car-bombing, says a gang connected with a current security scandal were involved in his killing.
- The conservative junior coalition partner is concerned over the high number of Islamists proposed for governor posts.
- The chairman of the DISK trade union says a security scandal linking the state with underworld gangs cannot be covered up.
- Representatives of the American credit rating agency Duff and Phelps are due to come to Turkey on January 23.
- The far-right Grand Unity Party withdraws its support from the ruling Islamist party.
